The paper presents a method for reducing the radar cross section of conducting objects using multiple passive impedance loadings.
The method uses the moment method and biquadratic programming to optimize the loadings and minimize the radar cross section.
The results show that multiple loadings are more effective than single loadings in reducing the radar cross section.
The radar cross section can be reduced to almost zero with multiple loadings.
The backscattering cross section becomes quite small for all directions of incident waves in the horizontal plane.
The intrinsic impedance of free space is used in the calculation of the bistatic radar cross section.
Biquadratic programming is used to optimize the loadings and minimize the radar cross section.
The moment method is used to calculate the current on the conducting object.
The paper considers conducting objects such as straight wires, circular loops, and rectangular wire frames.
The results show that the choice of the loading point is important.
Passive impedance loading is not effective if the load is put at a point of zero current.
The paper presents calculated and experimental results for a circular loop with two identical loads.
The results agree reasonably well.
